{
  "feasibility": {
    "verdict": "Partially feasible: single-column ELM resolves vertical (1-D) runoff generation processes at each site, but it cannot route or aggregate runoff between columns into streamflow.",
    "answerable": [
      "Vertical partitioning of precipitation into surface runoff (QOVER), subsurface drainage (QDRAI), infiltration, and evapotranspiration at each site",
      "Snowmelt-driven runoff timing and magnitude at the montane sites (seasonal hydrograph of QRUNOFF driven by SNOWMELT)",
      "Contrast in runoff-generation mechanism between the arid lowland column and the snow-dominated upland columns",
      "Soil moisture and water-table (ZWT) controls on saturation-excess vs infiltration-excess runoff"
    ],
    "not_answerable": [
      "Basin-integrated streamflow / discharge at a gauge (requires lateral river routing, e.g. MOSART, not single-column ELM)",
      "Spatial connectivity or timing of runoff propagation between the three columns",
      "Groundwater lateral flow between columns (single-column has no lateral subsurface exchange unless coupled to PFLOTRAN in a 3-D domain)"
    ]
  },
  "n_columns": 3,
  "n_justification": "User specified exactly three column locations; retained as-is. They span an environmental gradient from arid shrub-steppe lowland (~46.62,-119.90, near the Columbia confluence, low elevation) to snow-dominated Cascade uplands (46.85,-121.05 near White Pass and 47.02,-120.88 near the upper Naches), which is ideal for contrasting runoff-generation regimes.",
  "columns": [
    {"id": "NACHES_LOWLAND_ARID", "lat": 46.62, "lon": -119.90, "soil_texture": "sandy loam (arid shrub-steppe, infiltration-limited)"},
    {"id": "NACHES_HIGH_CASCADE", "lat": 46.85, "lon": -121.05, "soil_texture": "gravelly loam (montane forest, snow-dominated)"},
    {"id": "NACHES_UPPER_HEADWATER", "lat": 47.02, "lon": -120.88, "soil_texture": "loam (mid-elevation forest/meadow)"}
  ],
  "elm_config": {
    "DATM_CLMNCEP_YR_START": "1980",
    "DATM_CLMNCEP_YR_END": "2010",
    "STOP_N": "31",
    "RUN_STARTDATE": "1980-01-01",
    "hist_variables": [
      "QRUNOFF", "QOVER", "QDRAI", "QDRAI_PERCH", "QINFL", "QFLX_SURF",
      "RAIN", "SNOW", "QSNOMELT", "H2OSNO", "SNOW_DEPTH", "FSNO",
      "ZWT", "WA", "SOILLIQ", "SOILICE", "H2OSOI",
      "QVEGT", "QVEGE", "QSOIL", "EFLX_LH_TOT", "TSA", "TSOI",
      "QCHARGE", "FROST_TABLE", "RH2M"
    ]
  },
  "requires_capabilities": [
    "ELM single-column (PTS_MODE) point simulations",
    "GSWP3 (CLMGSWP3) atmospheric forcing 1980-2010 for each lat/lon",
    "Surface dataset generation (mksurfdata) at each point for PFT/soil",
    "VIC or default (TOPMODEL-based) hydrology option for runoff parameterization",
    "Optional ELM-PFLOTRAN coupling if explicit variably-saturated subsurface flow is desired"
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "Runoff generation is interpreted as 1-D column water-balance partitioning (QOVER + QDRAI), not routed streamflow.",
    "A 5-year spin-up (repeating 1980-1984 forcing) precedes the 1980-2010 analysis period to equilibrate soil moisture and snowpack; adjust STOP_N/RUN_STARTDATE if a separate spin-up run is used.",
    "Point (46.62,-119.90) lies in the arid Columbia lowland near, rather than within, the higher Naches basin and is treated as the dry end-member of the gradient.",
    "Default satellite phenology / BGC off unless carbon-water coupling is required.",
    "Surface and soil properties taken from ELM default surface dataset at each grid cell; texture labels are approximate site descriptors."
  ]
}

feasibility.verdict: Partially feasible: single-column ELM resolves vertical (1-D) runoff generation processes at each site, but it cannot route or aggregate runoff between columns into streamflow.
answerable: Vertical partitioning of precipitation into surface runoff (QOVER), subsurface drainage (QDRAI), infiltration, and evapotranspiration at each site
Snowmelt-driven runoff timing and magnitude at the montane sites (seasonal hydrograph of QRUNOFF driven by SNOWMELT)
Contrast in runoff-generation mechanism between the arid lowland column and the snow-dominated upland columns
Soil moisture and water-table (ZWT) controls on saturation-excess vs infiltration-excess runoff
not_answerable: Basin-integrated streamflow / discharge at a gauge (requires lateral river routing, e.g. MOSART, not single-column ELM)
Spatial connectivity or timing of runoff propagation between the three columns
Groundwater lateral flow between columns (single-column has no lateral subsurface exchange unless coupled to PFLOTRAN in a 3-D domain)

parsed.n_justification: User specified exactly three column locations; retained as-is. They span an environmental gradient from arid shrub-steppe lowland (~46.62,-119.90, near the Columbia confluence, low elevation) to snow-dominated Cascade uplands (46.85,-121.05 near White Pass and 47.02,-120.88 near the upper Naches), which is ideal for contrasting runoff-generation regimes.
requires_capabilities: GSWP3 (CLMGSWP3) atmospheric forcing 1980-2010 for each lat/lon
Surface dataset generation (mksurfdata) at each point for PFT/soil
VIC or default (TOPMODEL-based) hydrology option for runoff parameterization
Optional ELM-PFLOTRAN coupling if explicit variably-saturated subsurface flow is desired
assumptions: Runoff generation is interpreted as 1-D column water-balance partitioning (QOVER + QDRAI), not routed streamflow.
A 5-year spin-up (repeating 1980-1984 forcing) precedes the 1980-2010 analysis period to equilibrate soil moisture and snowpack; adjust STOP_N/RUN_STARTDATE if a separate spin-up run is used.
Point (46.62,-119.90) lies in the arid Columbia lowland near, rather than within, the higher Naches basin and is treated as the dry end-member of the gradient.
Default satellite phenology / BGC off unless carbon-water coupling is required.
Surface and soil properties taken from ELM default surface dataset at each grid cell; texture labels are approximate site descriptors.
